To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

multi task learning improves performance for both LU and for DST, scheduled sampling on DST output is beneficial, and scheduled sampling on LU improves performance for LU, but has a detrimental effect on DST

1) the proposed multi task learning approach outperforms single task learning on LU and DST, 2) DST with scheduled sampling on LU and DST outputs improves performance on DST, 3) DST with scheduled DST improves DST performance and 4) DST with scheduled LU and DST improves performance on both LU and DST.

(1) multi task learning of LU and DST improves performance over training LU and DST separately, (2) DST operating on candidate slot values generated by LU slot annotations, dialogue acts and the estimated dialogue state improves performance, and (3) scheduled sampling for the LU and DST output improves performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following three contributions: 1) a multi task learning framework that jointly trains a neural network for LU and DST; 2) a method to generate candidate sets for DST based on LU and DST annotations for previous turns; 3) an analysis of scheduled sampling for multi task learning.
two main questions: (i) How to jointly learn the two tasks? (ii) What is the best way to handle the candidate values during inference?
the development of a neural network architecture that can jointly learn to perform LU and DST, and with the use of scheduled training to bridge the gap to inference.

our proposed approach achieves significant improvement over the state-of-the-art in both LU and DST tasks.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present an end-to-end trainable model for multi-task learning of LU and DST in task-oriented dialogue systems, and we show that it outperforms the state of the art on both tasks.
we present a novel approach for joint learning of LU and DST, which is able to improve the performance for both tasks, while reducing the number network parameters.
we present a novel approach for the joint training of LU and DST in a task oriented dialogue system.

joint multi task learning for LU and DST improves both tasks, and scheduled sampling on LU and DST outputs during inference improves the dialogue state tracking task.
multi task learning is a viable option for jointly learning LU and DST.
